reasoning_traces.think:
The core mathematical framework integrates time-series forecasting with mixed-integer programming (MIP) to optimize daily fantasy sports teams. The prediction component models player performance using historical data, assuming stationarity and trend extrapolation. The optimization component uses a knapsack-like formulation where each player contributes a value (predicted points) and cost (salary), subject to budget and roster constraints. This dual structure creates a computationally tractable yet powerful abstraction of the DFS decision space. Dualities emerge in the trade-off between prediction accuracy and optimization robustness—when predictions are inaccurate, even optimal solutions may fail. Failure modes include overfitting in prediction models, constraint violations in optimization, and adversarial shifts in player availability or performance. The system's resilience depends on adaptive reweighting of prediction confidence and dynamic adjustment of optimization parameters. The framework supports recursive refinement through feedback loops where actual outcomes update predictive models, improving future decisions.
